bull_bear.body: Deleveraging is the priority and it is running on schedule: **INR1,250cr NCD tranche repaid in Q1**, net debt down to **INR3,377cr**, **0.9x** net debt/adjusted EBITDA, and the acquisition-related (BSV) debt still committed for **full repayment by FY28** — reconfirmed under direct questioning. Finance cost has already fallen INR32cr QoQ. Alongside that, capital is going into (i) capex at a guided 6–7% of revenue, (ii) R&D rising to 2.8–3.0% of sales, and (iii) bolt-on brand in-licensing (Rivotril from Roche). No dividend or buyback commentary. The cash-conversion drop to 77% from 99% is the item to watch against the FY28 repayment promise.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **West Asia crisis → gross-margin compression, flagged for next quarter.** The only stated reason for guiding 71%+ against 72.8% delivered. The inventory shield expires as cheap stock is consumed.
- **Structurally higher tax rate.** The Sikkim exemption is gone; ETR moved 17.7% → 25.4%. This is permanent and will keep PAT growth below EBITDA growth going forward.
- **GLP-1 — missed the first wave, entering into a price war.** Management admitted the miss plainly ("We could not launch in the first phase") and attributes it to being mid-restructuring. With **20+ companies and 35–40 brands** live and "a lot of price war happening at the moment", the strategy is a deliberately slow, KOL-led, therapy-bundled entry via two divisions (anti-diabetes and gynaec), with **no export strategy**. Management expects "a gradual take off".
- **Losing the new-launch race.** NI contribution 2.8% vs IPM 4.1%. Management's counter — selective launches made big (Vonalong #1 in vonoprazan; Empagliflozin top-3 among new launches) — is credible but does not close a 130bps gap.
- **Matching IPM, not beating it.** Management explicitly walked back the historical 1.2–1.3x (and once 1.7x) outperformance framing to an aspiration: "aspiration is to come back to where we were a few years back… It takes time. We are not in a hurry."
- **Cash conversion and working capital.** CF/EBITDA down to 77%; NOWC up 4 days. Management promises rationalisation by year-end — a checkable claim.
- **Consumer Healthcare is a self-inflicted drag.** The cash-and-carry exit cost growth (~3.8%) and an analyst pushed hard on why general trade did not pick up the slack; management's answer — that the channels are no longer separable and the market is soft — was honest but did not resolve the question.
- **Cash-EPS definition.** Non-standard vs peers; the difference is not trivial (~50% of INR225cr D&A is acquisition-related).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Unusually candid for a company mid-recovery. Rajeev Juneja twice declined the flattering framing on GLP-1, conceding "We could not launch in the first phase" and that the company was busy "correcting the overall company" — enforced attrition, people removed and replaced ~18 months ago. He also volunteered the discipline rule behind the numbers ("last week sales should not be there"), which is a claim about *quality* of secondary sales that an analyst can actually test. Prakash Agarwal corrected an analyst's premise with data rather than deflection (BSV grew "early teens" last year, not 5–6%) and supplied the covered-market series (56%→74%, rank 10→7) unprompted. Ashutosh Dhawan accepted the cash-EPS methodology challenge without defending it and offered to work the number offline. Against that: the Consumer Healthcare guidance was stated twice in two different forms within one answer ("high-teen to double-digit" then "high single-digit to double-digit") before being settled on follow-up, and the Denovo AI partnership was announced with no quantification whatsoever.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- **The acute recovery, not chronic, is what fixed this quarter.** Chronic is the strategic story, but acute is ~60% of the domestic book and it moved from 3.3% to 10.9% — arithmetically the larger contributor. The chronic mix only rose 80bps YoY (to 40%), so the 50% target implies roughly a decade at this pace, not the "4–5 years" stated.
- **Missing GLP-1 may have protected the P&L.** IPM's new-introduction contribution of 4.1% *includes* GLP-1s; Mankind's 2.8% excludes them. So part of the "growth gap" analysts are penalising is Mankind declining to buy revenue in a segment where price has already collapsed. Management's framing — "if we just play with the price war, this will not be a profitable launch", especially as they source from a partner — is an economic argument, not an excuse.
- **The margin beat is borrowed from inventory timing.** Price increases taken but not yet in COGS, plus a soft base. The CFO said the compression is coming next quarter and *still* held the EBITDA band — which means the 25.5–26.5% guide implicitly assumes cost offsets elsewhere, or that Q1's 26.3% is near the top of the year.
- **Below-guidance R&D and capex are a Q1 phasing artefact, not thrift.** Both ran under the FY27 guide. If the guides hold, the back three quarters carry a materially heavier spend load than Q1 — a reason not to annualise Q1's 26.3% margin.
- **BSV's independence is the integration strategy.** Management has resisted absorbing it — "run as an independent operationally, both in the domestic and international" — limiting itself to management tweaks and a biotech R&D upgrade. That caps synergy upside but also explains why BSV growth accelerated to 21% instead of stalling, which is the more common post-acquisition outcome.
- **Vistar is a distribution-capacity play disguised as a launch.** Creating a division to promote *existing* non-focus brands monetises field-force bandwidth freed by the attrition normalisation — growth without new molecules or new capex.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Deleveraging is the stated balance-sheet priority: net debt fell from INR 5,249 Cr at Jun-30-2025 through 4,791 (Sep-25), 4,294 (Dec-25) and 3,932 (Mar-26) to INR 3,377 Cr at Jun-30-2026.
- Net Debt/Adj. EBITDA of 0.9x per the Q1 FY27 snapshot (deck's at-a-glance slide states 1.1x for FY26); the leverage series printed on the chart is 1.4x, 1.3x, 1.1x, 0.9x and 1.6x.
- Cash generation: Cash Flow from Operations of INR 2,413 Cr in FY25 and INR 3,121 Cr in FY26, with "CFO to EBITDA" percentages of 80%, 89%, 99% and 77% shown on the same chart.
- Returns: FY26 ROCE of "12% / 41%" on an Inc. BSV / Exc. BSV basis (TTM, Adj. ROCE excludes the BSV acquisition); the ROCE chart also shows a 40-43% band alongside an 11-13% band flagged "With BSV Acquisition".
- Ownership: Promoters & Promoter Group 72.6%, FPI & Bodies Corporate 10.5%, Mutual Funds 13.8%, Retail 1.3%, Others 1.8%; free float 26.4% (free float = 100% - Promoters - Bodies Corporate) as on 30-Jun-2026.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Market position - #4 by value with market share of 4.7% and #2 by volume with market share of 6.1% in the Indian pharmaceutical market, and #1 in prescriptions over the last 9 years
- Distribution moat - one of the largest distribution networks in India with 17,600+ stockists, a field force of over 18,500 and the largest doctor coverage at 5 lakh+ doctors
- Manufacturing control - 75%+ in-house manufacturing across 32 modern facilities with 44+ billion units installed capacity, enabling high quality standards, timely deliveries and an efficient supply chain
- Supply-chain resilience - over 92% of raw materials procured locally, giving limited dependence on imports
- Quality credentials - 240+ DMF (Drug master file) / international-grade quality products launched in India for patients on prolonged medication
- Brand depth - 54/22/13 brands above Rs 50 / 100 / 200 crores, with a diversified therapy mix in which the top 5 contribute just 57% of overall sales
- Consumer healthcare franchise - four category-leading brands ranked 1 in their respective categories
- Super specialty entry barriers - the BSV specialty complex portfolio is characterised by high entry barriers and limited competition, and the Company emerged as the largest player in gynaecology with a 10.3% market share in FY 2025-26
- R&D base - 7 dedicated R&D facilities and 740+ scientists including ~110 PhDs
- Stated SWOT strengths - superior quality, affordability, accessibility, execution excellence, stronghold in the domestic market and pan-India presence
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Regulatory approval and compliance risk — The Board's cautionary statement lists government policies and regulations, obtaining regulatory approvals, and domestic and foreign healthcare reforms among the risks that may cause actual results to differ materially. As a pharmaceutical manufacturer, statutory compliance is evaluated monthly at each manufacturing site and quarterly at the corporate level under the Management Review Meeting and Committee/Board, indicating a continuous compliance burden across sites.
- Product safety and efficacy exposure — The cautionary statement explicitly flags 'claims and concerns about product safety and efficacy' as a risk to results, performance or achievements - a structural exposure for a company whose portfolio spans acute and chronic prescription therapies plus consumer healthcare products sold at scale.
- Competition and market conditions — Industry and market conditions and competition are named risk factors in the Board's cautionary statement. The Indian pharmaceutical industry has over 3,000 pharma companies, and the Company's own growth depends on holding share in therapies where multiple players compete on price and reach.
- Raw material availability and input supply — The cautionary statement lists 'unavailability of raw materials' among the risks that could materially change outcomes. Global supply chains are described as undergoing structural realignment, with businesses across pharmaceuticals diversifying sourcing to reduce concentration and geopolitical exposure.
- Execution risk on capacity build-out and managing growth — The cautionary statement names 'inability to build production capacity' and 'ability to manage growth' as risk factors - relevant given the Company's stated expansion into new therapies, super specialty and the integration of the BSV business acquired in October 2024.
- Currency, interest rate and macroeconomic volatility — Domestic and international economic conditions such as interest rate and currency exchange fluctuations, and political, economic, legal and social conditions in India and elsewhere, are named risk factors. Management separately flags rupee-dollar volatility as a channel through which the Middle East conflict could transmit.
- Geopolitical conflict and trade fragmentation — MD&A states the Middle East conflict poses a key downside risk to FY2027 through volatility in crude oil prices, disruption in overall energy supply, rupee-dollar volatility and global supply chain strain. Separately, broad-based tariff measures and retaliatory action have disrupted established global value chains, with the unpredictability of policy itself described as a material constraint on long-term investment decisions.
- Domestic market and distribution-channel concentration — India remained the key market, contributing 86% of consolidated revenue from operations in FY 2025-26, so the earnings base is concentrated in a single geography. The BRSR openness-of-business disclosure further shows that almost all sales route through dealers and distributors, and that a substantial share of purchases, loans and advances and investments is with related parties - structural concentrations even though they are not labelled as risks.

business.body:
- **Chronic (+15.8%, 40% of ex-BSV mix).** Cardiac **+19.4%** (Telmikind family ~+21%, Lipirose +30%, Statpure +31%); anti-diabetes **+12.7%** excluding tirzepatide, outperforming IPM 1.1x, with the Glizid family at **+29%**. Chronic respiratory has held **20%+ growth for four straight quarters**.
- **Acute (~60% of the domestic book).** The recovery is the quarter's central operational fact, and management gave the full sequential series: overall acute **3.3% (Q2 FY26) → 10.9% (Q1 FY27)**, now at par with industry. By therapy: gastro **-2.5% → 6.9% → 9.2% → 13.6%** (Pantakind at 1.8x IPM); vitamins **5% → 8% → 12.5% → 19.3%**; gynaec **6.9% → 12.7%** (IVF portfolio +39% in Foligraf and Humog, Dydroboon +20%); ophthalmology **6.2% → 14.9% → 18.5% → 17.5%**; anti-infectives **-1.1% (Q4 FY26) → +3.6%**.
- **Consumer Healthcare (INR246cr, ~+3.8%).** Deliberately depressed: management **stopped the discounted cash-and-carry channel** because it was cannibalising general trade. Market share still gained in **Manforce (condoms), Prega News (pregnancy tests) and Gas-O-Fast (antacids)**. The structural shift is the channel: **modern trade + e-commerce is now 15% of the mix, up from 11%, growing 38%**.
- **BSV (~+21% in Q1).** Run **operationally independent** by professionals; Mankind has tweaked management "wherever required" and **enhanced the R&D biotech facility**. Domestic ~+17%, international ~+25%, mix ~51:49. Demand-creation push on specialist brands (Anti-D, Foligraf, Histoglob): **gynaec coverage up from 33,000 (FY25) to 37,000**, **>80% coverage of the IVF category** which is growing **35%+**. Clinical programmes running: Foligraf (FSH) market-expansion trials, the **Rhythm study** on Anti-D, and **Histoglob** anti-allergy studies. International: **FSH approved in Russia**, with approvals expected in "a couple of new markets".
- **International ex-BSV.** US did well on a couple of launches; the historical one-off ophthalmic bulge is now fully in the base (bulged FY25, normalised FY26).
- **Vistar — new division launched** to scale lesser-focused brands sitting inside existing divisions. This is the third of four named growth levers (chronic mix, hospital penetration, new divisions for non-focus brands, under-penetrated states).
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- **Prescription leadership.** #1 in India with **15.2% prescription share** — management's framing is that this is the durable asset ("prescription is sales"), earned over decades through affordability and field execution, and the reason a field-force disruption showed up as a growth dip rather than a share collapse.
- **Volume-led, not price-led growth.** Secondary sales +12.7% on **volume +4.7%** (up 220bps YoY from 2.3%) — in a market where much reported IPM growth is price and new-introduction driven, volume share gain is the harder-won number.
- **Distribution reach as an acquisition multiplier.** The Rivotril logic — buy a small "textbook brand" purely for specialist-doctor entry — only works for a company that can then push volume through an existing field force.

business.body:
- "Consistently maintained #1 rank over last 9 years with prescription share of 15.2%" (as per IQVIA Jun 2026); ranks given as #2 by volume in IPM, #4 by value in IPM and #1 in Gynaecology.
- 4th largest pharma company in India with 4.7% market share (IQVIA MAT Mar'26); FY26 overall IPM rank #2 in Consumer/CVM terms with 4.7% MS and FY21-26 CAGR of 12.4% for Mankind vs 10.3% for IPM.
- Portfolio spans four layers - Mass Market (acute/chronic/semi-chronic), Specialty Chronic (cardio/diabeto/CNS), BSV Super Specialty (recombinants, niche biologics, novel delivery and immunoglobulins) and Consumer Healthcare (OTC) - each with its own targeted medical practitioners (GP/CP/MD/DM/KOL) and channels (GT/MT/ECOM).
- Scale markers: "54/22 Brand families worth INR 50/100 Cr+", FY26 revenue INR 14,278 Cr and 86% FY26 domestic revenue share; deck states "18,500+ Mar'26 Field force" (footnote: includes field managers) while the portfolio slide separately states "~16,800 Field Force".
- Category ranks by therapy (FY26): Chronic #3 (4.3% MS), Cardiovascular #4 (5.5%), Anti Diabetic #4 (4.5%), Acute #2 (5.0%), Anti-Infectives #5 (6.0%), Gynaecology #1 (10.3%), Gastro Int #6 (4.3%), Respiratory #6 (4.5%), VMN #2 (5.1%).
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Acquisition] 100% stake in BSV Limited acquired in 2024 and consolidated from 23-Oct-2024; almost every growth, margin, leverage and ROCE series in the deck is presented on both an including-BSV and excluding-BSV basis, and FY24/FY25 P&L items are for continuing operations only so prior-period numbers are "strictly not comparable".
- [Regulation - labour codes] Adjusted EBITDA and adjusted ROCE are struck after a "one time impact of labour code regulations and other non-recurring cost"; FY26 reported CH EBITDA is 18.3% versus the adjusted figure shown.
- [Regulation - EUGMP] Udaipur and Ambernath received EUGMP certification in 2025-26, and Paonta Sahib has been USFDA-inspected since 2018-19.
- [Base effect] Consumer Healthcare Q1FY27 growth of ~4% was "partly impacted by base effect of discontinued cash and carry business", though share was gained in Manforce, Preganews and Gas-o-fast.
- [Corporate history] Commenced operations in 1995 (founded 1991), entered chronic in 2004, entered consumer healthcare 2007-10 with Manforce and Prega News, first Indian company to launch Dydrogesterone, and listed on NSE and BSE in 2022.
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: The Company develops, manufactures and markets pharmaceutical formulations across a wide spectrum of acute and chronic therapeutic areas, together with a consumer healthcare portfolio, aimed at providing international-quality products at affordable prices accessible even in the remotest parts of the country. Its domestic franchise spans anti-infectives, cardiovascular, antidiabetic, gynaecology, gastrointestinal, VMN and respiratory therapies, with a stated strategy to increase chronic presence, while the acquired BSV portfolio adds branded specialty in women's health, fertility and critical care. Growth has been mostly organic, supplemented by brand acquisitions and in-licensing tie-ups with global innovators, and the international business is being expanded through branded specialty complex and niche drugs.

business.title: Group structure (profile)

business.body:
- Market position - #4 by value with market share of 4.7% and #2 by volume with market share of 6.1% in the Indian pharmaceutical market, and #1 in prescriptions over the last 9 years
- Distribution moat - one of the largest distribution networks in India with 17,600+ stockists, a field force of over 18,500 and the largest doctor coverage at 5 lakh+ doctors
- Manufacturing control - 75%+ in-house manufacturing across 32 modern facilities with 44+ billion units installed capacity, enabling high quality standards, timely deliveries and an efficient supply chain
- Supply-chain resilience - over 92% of raw materials procured locally, giving limited dependence on imports
- Quality credentials - 240+ DMF (Drug master file) / international-grade quality products launched in India for patients on prolonged medication
- Brand depth - 54/22/13 brands above Rs 50 / 100 / 200 crores, with a diversified therapy mix in which the top 5 contribute just 57% of overall sales
- Consumer healthcare franchise - four category-leading brands ranked 1 in their respective categories
- Super specialty entry barriers - the BSV specialty complex portfolio is characterised by high entry barriers and limited competition, and the Company emerged as the largest player in gynaecology with a 10.3% market share in FY 2025-26
- R&D base - 7 dedicated R&D facilities and 740+ scientists including ~110 PhDs
- Stated SWOT strengths - superior quality, affordability, accessibility, execution excellence, stronghold in the domestic market and pan-India presence
business.title: Competitive strengths

latest_quarter.body: Gross margin at 72.8% (+230bps) came from three named drivers in management's own order: **price increases taken**, **chronic mix up 120bps** (including BSV), and a **favourable base** from prior-year inventory accruals. Critically, the CFO was explicit that **the price increase has not yet flowed into COGS** because the company was sitting on comfortable inventory — which is exactly why NOWC rose to 52 days. That is a timing shield, and management said so: "the next quarter or so, we may see a compression in the gross margins level because the prices of the commodities and the dollar, et cetera, has increased." Below gross profit, only **20bps of the 250bps EBITDA gain came from operating leverage** — this was a gross-margin quarter, not a cost-efficiency quarter. Both R&D (2.4% vs 2.8–3.0% guided) and capex (4.9% vs 6–7% guided) ran *below* full-year guidance, which flatters Q1 margin and implies a spend catch-up in the remaining nine months.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
- **Q1 FY27 (this):** *(note: our previous note was Q3 FY26 — Q4 FY26 was not processed, so this entry spans two quarters.)* Revenue **INR4,031cr +12.9%**, EBITDA margin **26.3% (+250bps)**, PAT **INR574cr +29.1%**. The **workforce-transformation** thread from Q3 FY26 has closed out — attrition and vacancies "back to the normal level" after ~18 months of enforced correction, and the acute book has recovered from 3.3% (Q2 FY26) to **10.9%, level with IPM**. **Chronic outperformance** continues: +15.8%, chronic share 40% (+80bps), cardiac +19.4%. **BSV integration** is going well and stays deliberately independent — Q1 growth ~21% vs high-teens guided, FSH approved in Russia, IVF coverage >80%. **Digital OTC shift** confirmed and accelerating: modern trade + e-commerce now **15% of CHC from 11%, +38%** — but headline CHC growth only ~3.8% after the deliberate cash-and-carry exit. **GLP-1 preparation resolved unfavourably**: Mankind missed the first launch wave, has now entered via two divisions with a KOL/therapy strategy and no export plan, and expects "a gradual take off". New this quarter: **Vistar** division launched, **Rivotril** acquired from Roche, **Denovo Science** AI drug-discovery partnership, **Sikkim tax exemption expired** (ETR 17.7% → 25.4%), **INR1,250cr NCD repaid**, net debt **INR3,377cr / 0.9x**.
- _Q2 FY27 → check: did gross margin compress as warned and did the 71%+ / EBITDA 25.5–26.5% guides survive it; did Consumer Healthcare deliver the promised high single-digit to double-digit growth; did NOWC come down from 52 days and CF/EBITDA recover from 77%; are R&D (2.4% → 2.8–3.0%) and capex (4.9% → 6–7%) catching up to guidance; did NI contribution close the gap to IPM's 4.1%; is BSV holding high-teens; any progress on the FY28 acquisition-debt repayment; early read on the Semaglutide launch and Rivotril specialist traction._

outlook.body:
- **Revenue growth:** **double-digit** domestic growth for FY27, with "progressively outperforming IPM" over the remaining 9 months. Management was careful to disown a stronger claim: "we never said in last couple of quarters that we'll be beating the IPM."
- **Gross margin:** **upward of 71%** for FY27 — deliberately conservative against 72.8% delivered, with the *only* stated caveat being the **West Asia crisis** (commodity and dollar prices). Management warned of **gross-margin compression as soon as next quarter**.
- **EBITDA margin:** **25.5%–26.5%** for FY27, explicitly reaffirmed as unchanged and "reliable" despite the raw-material caveat.
- **Consumer Healthcare:** **high single-digit to double-digit growth from Q2 FY27 onwards** (Rajeev Juneja first said "high-teen to double-digit", then immediately corrected to "high single-digit to double-digit"; Prakash Agarwal confirmed the lower version on a follow-up — use the corrected figure).
- **BSV:** **high-teens ("high double-digit") growth** for FY27, in constant currency. Q1 ran at ~21%. Domestic:international mix to stay **~51:49, ±2%**.
- **Chronic mix:** currently **40%** (ex-BSV), targeting **50% over the next 4–5 years**.
- **R&D:** **2.8%–3.0% of sales** for FY27 (Q1 ran below at 2.4%).
- **Capex:** **6%–7% of revenue** for FY27 (Q1 ran below at 4.9%).
- **Debt:** **acquisition-related debt fully repaid by FY28**.
- **Working capital:** inventory to rationalise and NOWC days **to come down by year-end**.
outlook.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)

outlook.body: Not an order-book business. The forward-visibility proxies given were: prescription leadership (**#1, 15.2% prescription share**), the **IQVIA secondary sales series** (+12.7% with volume +4.7%), and the covered-market expansion story — in anti-diabetes, covered market rose from **56% in FY21 to 74% in FY26**, with rank improving from **10 to 7** and market share at **4.5%**. Management's own diagnosis of the growth gap is refreshingly specific: **new-introduction (NI) contribution was 2.8% against IPM's 4.1%** — i.e. Mankind is under-indexed on new launches, and IPM's 4.1% *includes* the GLP-1 wave Mankind sat out.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body:
- **Hospital channel** — management stated market share here is "still significantly below our peers", framing it as the longest runway available.
- **Under-penetrated states** — geographies where Mankind's ranking sits below its national standing; an explicit share-gain target.
- **In-licensing / brand acquisition** — **Rivotril acquired from Roche** (CNS). Current IQVIA size only **INR20–30cr**; the stated logic is specialist-doctor access rather than immediate revenue, with an aspiration to "make a gold portfolio on the CNS side".
- **AI-led drug discovery** — partnership with **Denovo Science**. No spend, milestone or timeline disclosed.
- **Covered-market expansion** — insulins, DPP-4, SGLT2, respiratory inhalers and lipid-lowering products all added to a book that historically skewed to older molecules.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Sharpen focus on both Scale and Specialisation - expand the differentiated portfolio while enhancing the quality and sustainability of growth at scale in the core domestic business
- Build around four growth engines: base business, specialty chronic, BSV branded super specialty and OTC
- Strengthen the domestic business through selective field force realignment, portfolio consolidation, deeper doctor coverage, targeted launches and digital enablement
- Prioritise volume-driven growth in the domestic business rather than price-led growth
- Raise the chronic share of the portfolio, driven by cardiac and anti-diabetic, and improve it to 50% over the medium term
- Scale focus brands 'from good to great' with Rs 500+ crores potential, and work whitespace opportunities for new launches while consolidating market share in focus therapies
- Enter high-end specialisations through in-licensing partnerships and brand acquisitions with global innovators such as Novartis, AstraZeneca, Takeda and Roche
- Expand the in-licensing pipeline from China, building on partnerships for Insulin Degludec, Insulin Aspart and Sintilimab
- Advance differentiated in-house R&D tech platforms and expand formulation expertise in sterile Blow-Fill-Seal products, Ophthalmics, Nasal Delivery Systems and Complex Injectable Formulations
- Establish a best-in-class Drug Substance Biologics facility in Vadodara and build a global-standard drug product facility in biologics to de-risk and scale for future growth and cater to international markets
- Keep manufacturing predominantly in-house (over 75% of production) for stronger process control, consistency and compliance, with partner facilities under rigorous oversight and audits
- Strengthen the 'Quality by Excellence' (QbX) framework using Lean, Kaizen and Six Sigma, and digitise quality systems through LIMS, Document Management Systems, eBMR platforms and environmental monitoring tools
- Scale AI from pilots to enterprise-wide capability through partnerships with Microsoft and OpenAI, including agentic AI deployments across commercial and management functions
- Use machine learning to accelerate formulation development and analytics-driven tools to prioritise complex generics and biosimilars by market opportunity and development feasibility
- Deepen consumer connect and brand equity in Consumer Healthcare brands such as Manforce, Prega News and Gas-O-Fast
- Advance science-led engagement by strengthening capabilities across R&D, medical affairs and evidence-based marketing
- The routed text does not set out a dividend or reinvestment philosophy. A Dividend Distribution Policy is named in the governance snapshot alongside the Whistleblower/Vigil Mechanism Policy, Risk Management Policy, Code of Conduct for Board and Senior Management, Nomination and Remuneration Policy, Related Party Transactions and Material Related Party Transaction policy, the code of practices for fair disclosure of UPSI and the CSR Policy, with the full policies available on the Company's website; no payout ratio, buyback, debt or credit-rating intent is stated. The only capital-deployment signals present are structural rather than policy-level: the acquisition of Bharat Serums and Vaccines Limited and its overseas arms, and the decision, after management carried out a strategic review of ongoing capital projects following that acquisition, to suspend further development of BSV's Hyderabad greenfield manufacturing project as no definitive timelines or future course of action had been finalised. Governance oversight of capital allocation sits with a fully independent, four-member Audit Committee chaired by Ms. Vijaya Sampath.
- Committed to recycling 100% of plastic waste generated in operations, including the plastic packaging of its products; the Company has built an inventory of plastic waste produced by its products in the Indian market and collaborates with Waste Management Agencies on a geo-neutral model based on CPCB guidelines, ensuring disposal at authorised recycling facilities
- Extended Producer Responsibility applies and the Company is registered with CPCB under the Plastic Waste Management Rules, 2016; during FY 2025-26 it processed 4,503 MT of plastic waste for recycling and 4,269 MT for co-processing towards energy recovery against the CPCB target
- 100% of R&D investment is focused on improving the environmental and/or social impacts of products and processes; environment- and social-linked capex was 16% of total capex in FY 2025-26 (22% in FY 2024-25), directed at water and energy conservation / GHG reduction and employee wellbeing and safety initiatives
- Sustainable sourcing programme covered 41% of procurement by value in FY 2025-26, backed by a procurement policy and a Third-party Code of Conduct (TCOC) setting ESG expectations for suppliers and value chain partners across business integrity, environmental responsibility, human rights, health and safety, employee wellbeing and fair labour practices
- ESG screening of all significant suppliers has been initiated, designed on the basis of the Third-party Code of Conduct
- Value chain partner engagement - more than 8 awareness sessions held on Environment, Health & Safety, Sustainability and BRSR, covering 44% of value chain partners by value of business done
- SGS India Pvt Ltd is engaged as the external assurance provider for the BRSR, with relevant policy implementation evaluated during the assurance audit process
- 100% training and awareness coverage on NGRBC Principles P1-P9 for the Board of Directors, Key Managerial Personnel, employees (7,153 programmes) and workers (1,195 programmes), covering business ethics, code of conduct, supplier conduct, ISMS, POSH, human rights, CSR, environment/safety and product quality and consumer health and safety
- Waste handling beyond plastics - E-waste generated at premises is disposed of through authorised recyclers per CPCB guidelines; hazardous waste is stored per regulatory requirement and disposed at authorised TSDF/recyclers/co-processing facilities; unsold end-of-life products are retrieved by warehouses for secure and responsible disposal; other manufacturing waste goes to authorised vendors for recycling, reuse or environmentally safe disposal
- Formal Life Cycle Assessments have not been undertaken for products; the Company incorporates energy efficiency, water efficiency, waste management and responsible sourcing into its environmental management practices and is evaluating the feasibility of implementing LCA methodologies for its key products
- Anti-corruption and anti-bribery are covered under the Code of Conduct and Business Ethics Policy applicable to all stakeholders, with the Code of Conduct published on the Company website
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The routed sections describe footprint and portfolio expansion rather than a named project pipeline. Mankind operates 32 modern manufacturing facilities and 7 dedicated R&D facilities with 5,000+ manufacturing personnel and 740+ scientists (of which ~110 hold PhDs), keeping 75%+ of manufacturing in-house, and reports an installed capacity of 44+ billion units across its globally accredited manufacturing facilities. Management states that over the last fiscal year it 'undertook calibrated capacity expansion, prioritised focus therapies and scale brands from good to great having ` 500+ crores potential', and is 'actively working on whitespace opportunities for new launches while consolidating market share in focus therapies'. Beyond physical capacity, expansion in this extract is inorganic and portfolio-led: the acquisition of Bharat Serums and Vaccines (BSV) for branded super specialty in women's health, fertility and critical care; brand acquisitions including Rivotril from Roche, Combihale, Daffy and brands from Panacea Biotech; and in-licensing tie-ups covering Symbicort (exclusive India distribution from AstraZeneca), Inclisaran and Vonoprazan alongside deals with Novartis, Biocon, Innovent Biologicals and Takeda. Stated forward expansion levers are increasing chronic presence (Empagliflozin, Insulin Glargine, respiratory inhalers), entering new therapies such as CNS and urology, deepening penetration in Metros/Tier I cities through KOL engagement, hospital tie-ups and specialty division launches, adding alternative channels including modern trade, and building on the BSV R&D tech platform for high entry barrier complex products. Distribution reach already spans 17,600+ stockists, a field force of over 18,500 and 5 lakh+ doctor coverage, with over 92% of raw materials procured locally. No greenfield or brownfield plant project, capex outlay, commissioning date or site-level capacity addition is disclosed in the routed sections.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Management expects improving domestic momentum to continue, 'driven by - existing brands, renewed focus on hospital channel, new launches and improving productivity'
- Acute therapies still form 60%+ of the domestic pharma business and were disrupted by transformational initiatives, but key therapies such as Gastro-Intestinal, Vitamins and Gynaecology are showing improving trends over the last few quarters
- Volume growth improved to 2.3% in FY2026 from 0.5% in FY2025 as restructured teams stabilised and processes were revamped
- Chronic share rose 190 bps in FY2026 to 39% excluding BSV, driven by strong growth in cardiac and anti-diabetic, and is expected to improve to 50% over the medium term
- BSV delivered double-digit growth on the domestic front driven by expansion of Gynaec coverage and continued focus on the IVF portfolio
- Entering FY2027 with a stronger foundation, a balanced portfolio and multiple growth engines across base business, specialty chronic, BSV and OTC, though the external environment remains dynamic
- Indian pharmaceutical industry supported by resilient demand, continued expansion in chronic therapies and improving healthcare access, with increasing focus on advanced niche molecules
- Global pharmaceutical market estimated to grow at a 5-8% CAGR up to 2030, supported by new products and patent expiries including the growing impact of biosimilars
- Patent cliff opportunity - the US market alone is projected to lose more than USD 230 billion in revenue between FY2025 and FY2030, opening low-cost generic launches
- Industry shift towards specialty drugs, biologics, personalised medicine and RNAi-based therapeutics, with biosimilars gaining traction as cost-effective alternatives
- US market grew 5.7% YoY in CY2025 and is expected to grow at a similar 5.7% pace over CY2025 to CY2033 to reach USD 1 trillion
- Pharmerging market spending expected to grow by USD 121 Bn through 2030, aided by healthcare access advancements and favourable government initiatives
- Global supply chains realigning under the 'China plus one' shift and tariff-driven trade fragmentation, creating opportunities for economies such as India
- India expected to be the key swing factor - FY2027 GDP growth projected to decline to 6.9%, with the Middle East conflict a key downside risk via crude oil price volatility, energy supply disruption, rupee-dollar volatility and global supply chain strain
- Insulin Aspart has successfully completed Phase III and is advancing towards commercialisation in India
- One recombinant biosimilar in the IVF space (1st in India) is advancing to Phase III
- GPR-119 (NCE) for anti-obesity and metabolic disorders has progressed into advanced stages of Phase II clinical trials
- Novel Immunoglobulin for Anti-Microbial Resistance (AMR) advancing to Phase I clinical trials
- MKP11093 (JAK inhibitor) progressing to Phase I clinical trials
- A couple of products in NASH and dry eye segments progressed, intended to be first to file in India
- In-licensing pipeline being expanded from China, building on partnerships for Insulin Degludec, Insulin Aspart and Sintilimab
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: The turnaround management promised after the field-force purge is now visible in the numbers rather than the narrative: revenue +12.9% to INR4,031cr with EBITDA margin up **250bps to 26.3%** and PAT up **29.1%**, driven by chronic (+15.8%) and an acute book that has climbed back from 3.3% growth in Q2 FY26 to **10.9%, now level with IPM**. Deleveraging is running ahead of plan — net debt down to INR3,377cr (0.9x), acquisition debt still tracked for **full repayment by FY28**. The two honest blemishes are that Mankind is *matching* IPM rather than beating it (new-product contribution 2.8% vs IPM's 4.1%), and that it **missed the GLP-1 first wave** and is now entering a price war it says it will not fight.

risks.note: The Board's cautionary statement lists government policies and regulations, obtaining regulatory approvals, and domestic and foreign healthcare reforms among the risks that may cause actual results to differ materially. As a pharmaceutical manufacturer, statutory compliance is evaluated monthly at each manufacturing site and quarterly at the corporate level under the Management Review Meeting and Committee/Board, indicating a continuous compliance burden across sites.

The cautionary statement explicitly flags 'claims and concerns about product safety and efficacy' as a risk to results, performance or achievements - a structural exposure for a company whose portfolio spans acute and chronic prescription therapies plus consumer healthcare products sold at scale.

Industry and market conditions and competition are named risk factors in the Board's cautionary statement. The Indian pharmaceutical industry has over 3,000 pharma companies, and the Company's own growth depends on holding share in therapies where multiple players compete on price and reach.

The cautionary statement lists 'unavailability of raw materials' among the risks that could materially change outcomes. Global supply chains are described as undergoing structural realignment, with businesses across pharmaceuticals diversifying sourcing to reduce concentration and geopolitical exposure.
risks.risk: Raw material availability and input supply

risks.note: The cautionary statement names 'inability to build production capacity' and 'ability to manage growth' as risk factors - relevant given the Company's stated expansion into new therapies, super specialty and the integration of the BSV business acquired in October 2024.
risks.risk: Execution risk on capacity build-out and managing growth

risks.note: Domestic and international economic conditions such as interest rate and currency exchange fluctuations, and political, economic, legal and social conditions in India and elsewhere, are named risk factors. Management separately flags rupee-dollar volatility as a channel through which the Middle East conflict could transmit.
risks.risk: Currency, interest rate and macroeconomic volatility

risks.note: MD&A states the Middle East conflict poses a key downside risk to FY2027 through volatility in crude oil prices, disruption in overall energy supply, rupee-dollar volatility and global supply chain strain. Separately, broad-based tariff measures and retaliatory action have disrupted established global value chains, with the unpredictability of policy itself described as a material constraint on long-term investment decisions.

India remained the key market, contributing 86% of consolidated revenue from operations in FY 2025-26, so the earnings base is concentrated in a single geography. The BRSR openness-of-business disclosure further shows that almost all sales route through dealers and distributors, and that a substantial share of purchases, loans and advances and investments is with related parties - structural concentrations even though they are not labelled as risks.

meta.thesis: The turnaround management promised after the field-force purge is now visible in the numbers rather than the narrative: revenue +12.9% to INR4,031cr with EBITDA margin up **250bps to 26.3%** and PAT up **29.1%**, driven by chronic (+15.8%) and an acute book that has climbed back from 3.3% growth in Q2 FY26 to **10.9%, now level with IPM**. Deleveraging is running ahead of plan — net debt down to INR3,377cr (0.9x), acquisition debt still tracked for **full repayment by FY28**. The two honest blemishes are that Mankind is *matching* IPM rather than beating it (new-product contribution 2.8% vs IPM's 4.1%), and that it **missed the GLP-1 first wave** and is now entering a price war it says it will not fight.
